text:
BERT4Rec trains a bidirectional Transformer to reconstruct masked items and appends a reserved [MASK] token for next-item inference. The original paper also includes terminal-only masked training samples to improve task alignment. Mask proportion is dataset-dependent: reported optima were 0.6 for Beauty, 0.4 for Steam, and 0.2 for MovieLens datasets; 0.2 is not a universal optimum. Changing mask proportion changes both available context and supervision density. [Original paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690)

Loss normalization matters: the paper defines a mean over masked targets within each sequence; the released implementation divides total weighted cross-entropy by the number of valid masked targets across the batch. These weight variable-length histories differently. Averaging over all padded positions would additionally change gradient scale as mask density changes. [Original training code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FeiSun/BERT4Rec/master/run.py)

Experimental implication: first compare terminal-only masking against one random masked target per sequence, holding sampled histories, batch size, optimizer steps, loss reduction, and architecture fixed. This controls target count while testing target location/context; it cannot completely isolate alignment because random interior targets see right context. Then vary random-mask density separately, logging supervised tokens, sequence presentations, optimizer updates, and GPU seconds. Equal epochs do not imply equal supervision or compute. Report fixed-budget validation performance separately from convergence claims: the reproducibility study found severe default-budget undertraining, requiring up to 30× longer training for the original implementation in its MovieLens-1M experiment. Keep the prescribed 200-epoch/200-batch ceiling and pinned validation evaluator. [Replicability study](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2207.07483)
